vision_features.image_context: Close-up photograph of the upper surface of a single broad green leaf, likely a dicot. Three prominent veins and a fine network of secondary veins are clearly visible. The leaf fills nearly the entire frame.
vision_features.abnormalities:
1. LARGER IRREGULAR MARKS (center and left-center of leaf): Multiple irregular to roughly angular patches ranging from approximately 5–20 mm in their longest dimension. These marks have a tan-to-light-brown dry, papery central area, some of which appear partially collapsed or tissue is missing (small holes/tears visible). The borders of these larger marks are dark brown to nearly black, forming a distinct narrow rim approximately 1–2 mm wide. The surrounding tissue immediately outside the dark border shows a diffuse lighter yellow-green halo of varying size (roughly 5–15 mm wide). These marks are distributed mainly in the upper-center and mid-left portions of the leaf, roughly between or near the major veins.
2. SMALLER PINPOINT TO SMALL MARKS (scattered across entire leaf surface): Numerous small circular to slightly irregular spots, approximately 1–4 mm in diameter, scattered across most of the visible leaf area. These have a tan or light brown dry center, often with a dark reddish-brown to dark purple-brown narrow border. Some are surrounded by a faint pale green or yellow-green zone. These are distributed broadly but appear more concentrated in the upper half of the leaf.
3. PALE/YELLOW-GREEN DIFFUSE ZONES: Several areas of the leaf show irregular diffuse pale yellow-green discoloration (lighter than normal leaf color) without sharp borders, particularly around and between the larger marks. These range from approximately 10–30 mm across and blend gradually into the surrounding green tissue.
vision_features.absences: 1. No powdery or dusty coating of any color is visible on the leaf surface. 2. No raised, puffy, or blister-like structures are visible within or around any of the marks. 3. No visible thread-like or fuzzy growth on the leaf surface. 4. No dark tiny raised dots or pustule-like structures are clearly visible within the centers of the marks.
vision_features.summary: The leaf surface displays two categories of marks: numerous small (1–4 mm), circular tan-centered spots with dark reddish-brown borders scattered widely across the leaf, and several larger (5–20 mm), irregular tan-to-brown dry patches with a distinct dark brown-black border, some showing tissue loss or holes. Both types of marks are surrounded by diffuse pale yellow-green halos. The upper-center and mid-left areas of the leaf are most severely affected, where the larger marks are clustered. The most striking feature is the combination of the sharp, very dark (near-black) border rim surrounding the larger irregular dry patches alongside the conspicuous pale yellow-green halo zones around them.

Knowledge-base entry for 'Phyllosticta_leaf_spot':
────────────────────────────────────────
Lesions most often occur on leaves and are circular, oval, and irregular or V-shaped. Lesions appear gray or tan and have a narrow, dark margin. Irregularly shaped tan/brownish lesions with purplish margins may be observed in the lower canopy.. In older lesions, numerous small, black specks (i.e., pycnidia) may be visible.
────────────────────────────────────────

Knowledge-base entry for 'Phytophthora':
────────────────────────────────────────
Young plants show rapid yellowing and wilting with soft rot and collapse of the root. Mature plants exhibit general yellowing of lower leaves progressing upward, followed by wilting and death, with brown discolored roots and a dark chocolate-brown stem discoloration extending from below the soil line upward several nodes; leaves typically stay attached after plant death.. The best diagnostic symptom on susceptible varieties is a lower stem discoloration (dark chocolate-brown) that may extend several nodes up the stem. Root system shows lateral and branch roots almost completely discolored; tap roots with brown surface discoloration and tan to brown inner tissue discoloration. Leaves turn yellow, wilt, and typically stay attached after plant death.. stem canker, Pythium
────────────────────────────────────────

Knowledge-base entry for 'Tobacco_Streak_Virus':
────────────────────────────────────────
Symptoms include bud blight, shepherd's crooking, stunting, wilting, delayed maturity, bud and leaf proliferation, reduced pod number, discolored, distorted, and dead leaves, discoloration and dead streaks at nodes, dark spots on pods, and delayed seed development.. Pod lesions, proliferation of tissue, discoloration and dead streaks at nodes, dark spots on pods, and seed discoloration are characteristic features.
